requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
**Verdict: the requirement is met.** Every obligation has marked implementation code and test coverage, and the spelling is documented. I found no unacknowledged gaps.

**Implementation** (`src/outline/rust.rs`, all marked `{impl}`):
- `KINDS` maps these grammar nodes to outline kinds:
  - `function_item` and `function_signature_item` map to `fn`.
  - `struct_item`, `enum_item`, `union_item`, `trait_item` and `mod_item` map to `struct`, `enum`, `union`, `trait` and `mod`.
  - `impl_item` maps to `impl`.
  - `macro_definition` maps to `macro`, named by its `name` field. Item-position `macro_invocation` also maps to `macro`, but anonymous.
  - `const_item` and `static_item` map to `const` and `static`.
  - `type_item` and `associated_type` map to `type`.
  - `foreign_mod_item` maps to `extern`.
- `use_declaration` is `NameRule::Anonymous`, as the requirement says for `use` and other items without a suitable name.
- `impl_name` builds the name from the syntactic `type` field text plus the optional `trait` field text. That gives `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`, and generics are kept, as in `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`.
- `extern_name` uses the ABI string content and falls back to `Rust` when there is none.
- `item_macro` and `in_item_list` restrict macro nodes to item position. Expression macros inside function bodies stay transparent.
- Segments come from the syntactic ancestry inside one file. `mod[external]` is a leaf node, and nothing resolves a `mod x;` declaration to another file. The shared builder in `outline/mod.rs` and `selector.rs` is marked for `outlines` and `outline_selectors`. It supplies nesting, percent-encoding and `#N` disambiguation.
- `PROFILE` is marked for this requirement.

**Documentation:** `md/requirements/references.md` has the examples `selector_nested`, `selector_impl_and_trait`, `selector_inline_and_foreign`, `selector_duplicate_names` and `selector_use`. `md/reference.md` has an "Outline profiles" table. The table gives the Rust kind, grammar node and name rule for each mapped node, and the bullets under it explain attachment. Together these document the selector spelling.

**Tests** (`src/outline/tests.rs`):
- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` checks every required item kind, plus:
  - nested `mod[local]/fn[run]` and `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`;
  - `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`, and an impl on an odd type, `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`;
  - trait methods and the associated type;
  - `extern[C]` and `extern[Rust]`;
  - duplicate names as `#1` and `#2`;
  - a macro definition, union, enum, const, static, type alias and extern crate.

  It also checks that each selector resolves to its own node, and that an ambiguous or missing selector is an error.
- `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` checks that `use` declarations are anonymous (`use@…`) and distinct, plus the same ancestry cases.
- `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` checks that item macros get anonymous `macro@<12 hex>` selectors, including inside an impl and a mod, and that macros inside function bodies are not nodes. It also checks a generic impl name, `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`.

**Possible concerns, none blocking:**
- The profile also emits `extern-crate[name]` nodes, which the requirement does not list. That kind has a name, so it fits the general scheme. It is documented in the profile table, and tested.
- There is no explicit test that a separate-file `mod x;` is left unresolved. The `mod[external]` leaf case covers this indirectly, and the code has no cross-file logic.

The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
